title: Performance tests: TTFT, tails and realistic workloads
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects performance tests: ttft, tails and realistic workloads with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Produce a load report with p50/p95/p99, TTFT, success rate, throughput and mode.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: TTFT measures time to the first generated token; end-to-end latency measures completion; tokens per second describes generation rate. p50, p95 and p99 summarize latency distributions. Throughput counts completed tasks per unit time, while concurrency counts in-flight tasks. These quantities answer different capacity questions.
Load tests need representative prompt length, retrieval work, output length, cache state and provider limits. Short fixture responses test service mechanics, not live-model generation capacity.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use k6 or a controlled client with bounded arrivals, correlation IDs and separate latency measurements. Include cold and warm runs, slow streaming clients, rate limits and long context. Report offered load, accepted load, error rate and completed throughput.

Avoid coordinated omission: a client that waits for each slow response before sending the next request hides overload. Set acceptance thresholds before testing and retain raw samples for tail analysis.
sections.code:
import math
def percentile(values,p):
    v=sorted(values)
    return v[max(0,math.ceil(p/100*len(v))-1)]

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Average latency looks acceptable while a small group waits thirty seconds. A benchmark excludes failed requests from percentiles and claims a faster system after an outage. A fixture is advertised as provider performance.
Test percentile implementation, record timeout outcomes explicitly and compare the same workload/configuration. Identify whether saturation occurs in queueing, retrieval, network or generation.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Produce a load report with p50/p95/p99, TTFT, success rate, throughput and mode. A release must meet both latency and quality contracts under the specified load.

For SDETs, capacity assertions should be reproducible within a documented environment. External provider variability needs repetitions and clear limitations; deterministic service limits can be tested directly.

takeaway: Produce a load report with p50/p95/p99, TTFT, success rate, throughput and mode.

title: Load-test interpretation and coordinated omission
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects load-test interpretation and coordinated omission with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance states workload, mode, success rate, latency tails and throughput.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A closed-loop client waits for responses before sending more work, which is useful for bounded service smoke tests but can hide queue pressure during slow periods. An arrival-rate workload schedules requests independently of completions and better exposes overload, while requiring careful admission and resource controls.
Provider TTFT requires streaming event timing. A local extractive endpoint returning one JSON payload cannot establish generation TTFT or tokens-per-second performance.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Run the supplied bounded load client and label its mode as local extractive service. Record count, concurrency, errors, successful throughput and raw latency samples. Use a k6 constant-arrival-rate experiment for capacity testing when the environment supports it.

Include long and short inputs, cache states and slow dependencies. Separate queue delay from service execution and define whether rejected/time-out requests count in each reported statistic. Keep quality checks under load so fast invalid responses do not look successful.
sections.code:
python local-labs/performance/load.py --count 50 --concurrency 5
# This is a bounded closed-loop local-service measurement

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Increasing concurrency lowers reported latency because failed requests are dropped. A tiny fixture endpoint is compared with a live model and described as a model speedup. A benchmark reports only p50 and misses a severe p99 tail.
Test the metric calculation with known samples, inspect errors and repeat the same workload. State the client scheduling model and environment so a reader can interpret its limits.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance states workload, mode, success rate, latency tails and throughput. A capacity claim requires the production-like dependency path and a suitable arrival model, not only a smoke script.
SDETs should connect load thresholds to user outcomes and identify where saturation occurs. Preserve failure samples and trace IDs rather than averaging the service into a single favorable number.

quiz.question: Can a non-streaming extractive fixture measure live-model TTFT?
options: No: it measures a different execution path
Yes: every first byte is a generated token
quiz.explanation: TTFT requires the actual generation stream and its token events.
